newsitem.title: USA: News Corp says Fox Filmed led U.S. results.
newsitem.headline: News Corp says Fox Filmed led U.S. results.

text.p: News Corp said Wednesday its Fox Filmed Entertainment posted a 154 percent gain in operating profits for the six months ending December 31, 1996, leading results in its U.S. operations.
The gain reflected the continued success of the film Independence Day, which since being released in July has generated more than US$787 million in worldwide box office receipts, it said.
It said 21 million copies of the Independence Day video have been ordered since its domestic release in November.
However, it said the gains were offset by poor performance of several of the company's recent releases, including Jingle All and Way and The Crucible.

This past weekend, Fox re-released George Lucas' classic, Star Wars, raking in US$36 million in ticket sales, a record for any film released in January. Later this quarter, Fox will re-release the second and third instalments of the original Star Wars trilogy.
Total operating profits of the News Corp group were up 15 percent over last year to US$706 million against $614 million a year ago, it said.
It did not provide a breakdown of company by company operations, but said it filmed entertainment, magazine and inserts and U.K. newspaper operations made solid gains in operating income.
U.S. television and book publishing were off against last year, it said. The book division's education division was sold in March 1996.
In the United Kingdom, its newspaper operations continued to post strong growth, with an 18 percent rise in operating profits on a year-on-year basis, it said.
Also contributing to the increase in U.S. profitability were earnings gains at News Digital Systems Ltd, arising from growth in worldwide demand for its products and technologies, it said.
Earnings for Australian newspaper oeprations increased slightly on a year-on-yar basis after improvement in the December quarter, it said.
As its STAR TV operations continued a regional expansion, losses at the pan-Asian satellite broadcaster were in line with expectations, it said.
Among associated companies, BSkyB, its British pay television operation, continued its robust growth, with after-tax profits rising 27 percent to 121 million pounds sterling.
Fox/Liberty Networks, a worldwide sports programming joint venture between News Corp and Liberty Media Corp, was successfully launched in November, it said.

It said its Japan Sky Broadcasting venture is expected to begin operations in 1997, pending government approval, with a package of 14 digital channels, which will be expanded to 150 channels by April 1998.
